title: Irkutsk Plague Watch
pathogen: Unconfirmed — officially pneumonia of undetermined etiology; Yersinia pestis named by the head of Buryatia (later amended to 'possibly') and suspected in media reports; Irkutsk officials speak only of an especially dangerous infection.
pathogen_note: Yersinia pestis is a bacterium, not a virus, and it responds to antibiotics when treatment starts early; some early reports used the word virus loosely.
origin_label: since the reported test-tube break on 25 Sep, which officials have not confirmed
method_note: Figures checked against 18 web searches in Russian and English. No Rospotrebnadzor or Health Ministry statement dated 6 October evening or 7 October was found; 6 October federal and regional items (Lenta, Shkulev network, AiF Irkutsk, Interfax) repeat the 5 October 60% figure, so counts are carried forward with counts_as_of 2026-10-05. The 197 / 189 base was re-seen in Lenta, Doctor Piter and Washington Times but remains media-sourced. WHO statements taken from UN News with Global News, The National, Korea Times and Tribune/ANI corroboration; the three-tier risk grading was visible only in UN News. ECDC item read from the ECDC site. US Embassy alert from the TravelGov post and ru.usembassy.gov page. The EU HSC meeting rests on a single Euronews report. The 10-day staff consultation detail was not visible in snippets and is flagged as reported. Alarmist headlines (Newsweek, My.ua, Vision Times, ETV Bharat, MSK1 doctors' account, Euronews quarantine piece) excluded. Aggregator sites excluded.
status_note: As of 7 October the official figures are unchanged from Rospotrebnadzor's 5 October release (observation completed for 60% of contacts; 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases, no other pathogens), the diagnosis remains pneumonia of undetermined etiology and the 197 / 189 contact base remains media-sourced. On 6 October Russia told WHO that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk and that no high-threat pathogens were found among contacts, but WHO says the pneumonia pathogen has not been identified; ECDC published its first item, WHO gave graded risk levels (Irkutsk moderate to low, Russia low, WHO European Region very low), the US Embassy issued a health alert and the EU Health Security Committee discussed the case on 7 October.

series.note: Media reports, citing the Telegram channel Mash, that a laboratory assistant broke a test tube holding the plague pathogen at the institute on this date. Rospotrebnadzor said on 4 Oct that its biosafety and expert commissions found no accidents in work with pathogenic micro-organisms at the institute. No official figures exist for this date.
series.note_short: Media reports, citing the Telegram channel Mash, that a laboratory assistant broke a test tube holding the plague pathogen at the institute on this date.

series.note: Media reports that the worker first felt unwell on this date and told relatives her condition was worsening. No official timeline has been published. No new figure; carried forward.
series.note_short: Media reports that the worker first felt unwell on this date and told relatives her condition was worsening.

series.note: Media reports that she was admitted to Shelekhov District Hospital with severe pneumonia, treated at first as suspected severe COVID-19, and placed on a ventilator. No official figure; carried forward.
series.note_short: Media reports that she was admitted to Shelekhov District Hospital with severe pneumonia, treated at first as suspected severe COVID-19, and placed on a ventilator.

series.note: Shelekhov District Hospital suspended admissions and discharges in several departments from this date, announced by the district mayor. No contact figures were published yet; carried forward.
series.note_short: Shelekhov District Hospital suspended admissions and discharges in several departments from this date, announced by the district mayor.

series.note: The worker died in the early hours of 2 Oct. Governor Kobzev reported a suspected case of an especially dangerous infection, held an extraordinary sanitary commission with Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova, and said all identified contacts were under observation with no signs of illness and negative laboratory results. Izvestia, citing unnamed sources, gave 197 contacts identified and 189 hospitalised for preventive observation, split 114, 63 and 12 across three facilities, with eight observed at home; officials gave no number of their own. Some outlets rendered this as 197 hospitalised, which merges the two figures. The head of Buryatia named plague as the cause and later amended his post to say possibly plague.
series.note_short: The worker died in the early hours of 2 Oct. Governor Kobzev reported a suspected case of an especially dangerous infection; media put contacts at 197, with 189 in hospital.

series.note: No new figure; carried forward. IrkutskMedia's morning roundup restated 197 contacts, 189 hospitalised and eight outside hospital, and said no reports of new cases had been received.
series.note_short: IrkutskMedia's morning roundup restated 197 contacts, 189 hospitalised and eight outside hospital, and said no reports of new cases had been received.

series.note: No new contact count; carried forward. Rospotrebnadzor gave the diagnosis as pneumonia of undetermined etiology, said expanded testing of her samples found no micro-organisms linked to her work, and said no contact showed health changes linked to infectious pathology; testing of contacts found two cases of COVID-19 and two of rhinovirus infection and no other pathogens. The agency described the situation in Irkutsk Oblast and in Irkutsk and Shelekhov as stable and gave no contact count of its own; the roughly 200 under observation cited in some coverage is a media figure (Radio Svoboda The symptomatic count stays 0: it counts only contacts with symptoms or a positive test for Yersinia pestis or the suspected especially dangerous infection, and the two COVID-19 and two rhinovirus positives reported this day are excluded as unrelated to the suspected pathogen (RIA Novosti
series.note_short: Rospotrebnadzor gave the diagnosis as pneumonia of undetermined etiology, said testing of her samples found no micro-organisms linked to her work, and called the situation stable.

series.note: No new figure; carried forward. No Rospotrebnadzor statement dated 5 October was found; the 4 October statement (pneumonia of undetermined etiology, no micro-organisms linked to her work, all identified contacts under observation with negative laboratory results, two COVID-19 and two rhinovirus cases) remains the latest official word. The 197 / 189 contact figures remain media-sourced (REN TV via Izvestia, repeated by Meduza on 5 Oct as 114 + 63 + 12 at the institute); no official count, release or discharge figure has been published. New context: regional outlet IrCity reports the Shelekhov district hospital inpatient block still closed while the Shelekhov polyclinic works normally, and that Irkutsk city hospitals operate normally, with the Ivano-Matreninskaya children's hospital denying a quarantine on 4 Oct; fact-check outlets (voynasfeykami.rf, spbnews78) call the four-hospital three-week quarantine report false, while The Insider and Meduza say hospitals confirmed restrictions to journalists. A US State Department official said on 4 Oct the US is monitoring with the CDC; a White House official told Axios it is 'assessing options'. A criminal case under Article 236 was reported by Rambler on 2 Oct; the investigating body is not named.
series.note_short: No new figure; carried forward. No new official statement; US government says it is monitoring; Shelekhov inpatient block still closed per regional media.

series.note: First official release figure. Rospotrebnadzor (via Interfax, 5 Oct; repeated by OGIRK and NIA Ekologiya on 6 Oct) says medical observation has been completed for 60% of contacts, decided on laboratory results and health status. No absolute count was given; under_observation is kept at the media-sourced 197 base as an unchanged carry-forward, since no outlet reports a new count. Applying the 60% to that base would give about 118 released and about 79 remaining, but both figures are derived rather than reported and are not in the series. The hospitalized figure of 189 is carried forward unchanged; no official discharge figure has been published. The same Rospotrebnadzor statement reports screening found 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases among contacts and no other infectious-disease pathogens, with contacts' health unchanged; these are incidental infections, so symptomatic for the suspected pathogen stays 0. Yersinia pestis remains neither named, confirmed nor excluded; the diagnosis is still pneumonia of undetermined etiology, so confirmed stays 0. On 6 Oct the regional Rospotrebnadzor directorate called a circulating document about an enhanced sanitary-epidemiological regime a fake, said no restrictions have been decided, and said a biosafety oversight commission found no emergencies in work with pathogens at the institute; an expert commission sent on the instruction of Rospotrebnadzor leadership confirmed that finding and a check of institute staff found no health changes linked to infectious pathology. WHO (spokesperson Christian Lindmeier) says it is in contact with Russian authorities to verify the event and laboratory tests and assesses the risk to the general population as low based on unofficial information; this is a press statement, not a Disease Outbreak News item. Regional media report the Shelekhov hospital quarantine still in force on 6 Oct.
series.note_short: Rospotrebnadzor says observation completed for 60% of contacts (no absolute count; 197 / 189 base carried forward unchanged, about 79 remaining if derived); 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus found among contacts, no other pathogens.

series.note: No new figure; carried forward. Rospotrebnadzor's latest substantive figures remain the 5 October release (observation completed for 60% of contacts; 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases among contacts, no other pathogens; no microorganisms linked to the worker's professional activity found in her samples), repeated by federal and regional outlets on 6 October with no absolute contact, release or remaining count. The 197 / 189 base is still media-sourced. New context on 6 October: Russian authorities replied to WHO that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk and that the illness first presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection; WHO says Russia has not identified the pneumonia pathogen and has asked for it. WHO gave graded risk levels (Irkutsk moderate to low, Russia low, WHO European Region very low). ECDC published its first news item on 6 October (no secondary cases, no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission). The US Embassy in Russia issued a health alert on 6 October. The EU Health Security Committee discussed the case at a scheduled meeting on 7 October. Governor Kobzev said on 5 October that no new cases of institute staff seeking medical care had been identified, and the regional government press service said all Irkutsk hospitals operate normally. No report of the Shelekhov hospital inpatient block reopening.
series.note_short: No new figure; carried forward. Russia told WHO on 6 October that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk but has not named the pathogen; ECDC published its first item and WHO issued graded risk levels.

timeline.source_name: Lenta.ru, citing the Telegram channel Mash
timeline.text: Media reports, citing the Telegram channel Mash, that a laboratory assistant broke a test tube containing the plague pathogen at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute and felt unwell soon after. Rospotrebnadzor said on 4 October that no accidents in work with pathogenic micro-organisms were found at the institute.
Media reports that the worker first felt unwell on this date and hoped it was a seasonal cold. No official timeline has been published.
Media reports that she was admitted to Shelekhov District Hospital with severe pneumonia, treated at first as suspected severe COVID-19, and placed on a ventilator.
Shelekhov District Hospital suspended admissions and discharges in several departments, a step announced by the district mayor and later referred to by the governor.

The worker died in the early hours of the day. Governor Igor Kobzev said information had appeared about a suspected case of an especially dangerous infection and held an extraordinary sanitary and anti-epidemic commission with Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova, who travelled to Irkutsk.
Kobzev said all identified contacts were under medical observation, showed no signs of illness and had negative laboratory results.

Media reports, citing unnamed sources, that 197 contacts were identified, 189 of them placed in hospital for preventive observation across three facilities, with eight isolated at home. No official body has published these numbers.

The head of Buryatia, Alexey Tsydenov, named plague as the cause of death and said the woman had not visited his republic. He later amended the post to say possibly plague; no Irkutsk official used the word, speaking instead of an especially dangerous infection.
Media report a criminal case opened under Article 236 of the Criminal Code (violation of sanitary-epidemiological rules negligently causing death). The investigating body is not named.

The Baikalsk town administration posted, then deleted about two hours later, a Telegram advisory asking residents to limit visits to Shelekhov pending clarification of unofficial information about a plague case.
The general director of the IrkAZ aluminium plant in Shelekhov announced a mask regime at the plant on his Telegram channel; most coverage followed on 4 October.
The Baykalsk town administration asked residents to limit travel to Shelekhov and nearby settlements, then removed the post less than two hours later.

Media reports, citing healthcare-sector sources, that five Irkutsk medical facilities were placed under a three-week quarantine. The Insider confirmed by phone a ban on visiting inpatients at three city hospitals; the children's hospital gave conflicting answers and the maternity hospital was not confirmed. A pro-government fact-check channel called the mass-quarantine reports false. No regional health ministry or Rospotrebnadzor comment on these measures was found.

Rospotrebnadzor gave the diagnosis as pneumonia of undetermined etiology, said no micro-organisms linked to the worker's professional activity were found in her samples and no accidents were recorded at the institute, reported two cases of COVID-19 and two of rhinovirus infection among tested contacts and no other pathogens, and called the situation in Irkutsk Oblast and in Irkutsk and Shelekhov stable.

A US State Department official said the US is aware of reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast and is monitoring with the CDC and interagency partners, urging Russia to share accurate information quickly and openly. No travel restrictions were announced.

The Ivano-Matreninskaya children's hospital denied it was under quarantine. Fact-check outlets (voynasfeykami.rf, spbnews78) labelled the report that four Irkutsk hospitals were closed for three weeks as false, while The Insider and Meduza report that hospitals No. 1, 3 and 10 and a maternity hospital confirmed restrictions to journalists.

WHO told CNN it is in contact with Russian health authorities to verify the event, its circumstances, the laboratory tests under way and their results, and that the risk to the general population appears low based on unofficial information.
A White House official told Axios the administration is aware of the suspected outbreak, is monitoring it and is 'assessing options'.

Regional outlet IrCity reports the Shelekhov district hospital inpatient block remains closed while the Shelekhov polyclinic takes planned and emergency patients, and that Irkutsk city hospitals operate normally. No new Rospotrebnadzor statement was found; the agency's 4 October position stands.

Rospotrebnadzor's press service said medical observation had been completed for 60% of the contacts of the deceased employee, on the basis of laboratory results and their state of health, and that the sanitary-epidemiological situation in Irkutsk Oblast is calm. Screening of contacts found 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other infectious-disease pathogens; contacts' health status was unchanged. No absolute count was given and Yersinia pestis was not named.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Rospotrebnadzor is the competent agency and urged people to rely on its official statements rather than rumours.

WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said WHO is in contact with Russian health authorities to verify the event, the laboratory tests and their results, the rationale for contact tracing and the health status of contacts, and that based on unofficial information the public-health risk to the general population appears low. This is a press statement, not a Disease Outbreak News item.
President Trump told reporters at the White House the US is ready to help Russia with the suspected case if asked and that he had not spoken to Putin about it.

European Commission spokesperson Eva Hrnčířová said the Commission is aware of reports of a laboratory incident in Russia seemingly involving a plague pathogen, is in touch with ECDC experts, is monitoring closely and uses WHO channels for updates. No ECDC publication has been found.

Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health said it is monitoring the Irkutsk situation, has strengthened sanitary-quarantine control at border crossings, assesses the risk of importation as low and has detected no travellers with fever or signs of illness.
RFE/RL reported, without an official figure, that more than 60 staff of the Anti-Plague Institute had been isolated after the worker's death.
Governor Igor Kobzev said no new cases of Anti-Plague Institute staff seeking medical care had been identified.

The Irkutsk Oblast government press service said all hospitals in Irkutsk are operating in normal mode and called reports of four hospitals, including the children's hospital, being closed for three weeks a fake.

Rospotrebnadzor's Irkutsk directorate declared a circulating document announcing an enhanced sanitary-epidemiological regime and strict restrictions in the region to be fake, said no decisions on restrictions have been taken, said the situation in Irkutsk and Shelekhov is calm, and said a biosafety oversight commission found no emergency situations in work with pathogenic microorganisms at the institute.

Rospotrebnadzor said an expert commission sent to the Anti-Plague Institute on the instruction of its leadership confirmed the biosafety commission's finding of no accidents with pathogenic microorganisms, and that examination of institute staff showed no health changes linked to infectious pathology.
Regional media report the Shelekhov hospital quarantine remains in force despite Rospotrebnadzor's denial of regional restrictions.

IrCity reports the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute is going ahead with an international conference on plague distribution on 21 and 22 October, planned before the incident; this is the first item indicating the institute is operating.

Russian health authorities replied to WHO's verification request, saying no case of plague has been recorded in Irkutsk, in the deceased or anyone else, that the illness first presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection, that identified contacts were placed under observation and tested, and that no high-threat pathogens were detected among contacts. WHO Director-General Tedros relayed the reply; spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said at the Geneva briefing that WHO has asked which pneumonia-causing pathogen caused the death and has not been told. WHO gave graded risk levels of moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia and very low for the WHO European Region.

ECDC published its first news item on the case, saying it is closely monitoring a case of pneumonia of unknown origin in eastern Russia suspected to be plague, that the suspicion is not confirmed, that there are no reports of secondary cases and no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission, and that there is little travel between Irkutsk and the EU.

The US Embassy in Russia issued a health alert saying it is aware of press reports of suspected pneumonic plague in Irkutsk and associated hospital measures, advising US citizens in Irkutsk Oblast to follow local health authority instructions and avoid affected medical facilities, and reiterating the existing Level 4 Do Not Travel advisory.

Rospotrebnadzor's consolidated statement, as carried by the Shkulev network, repeated that expanded testing of the worker's samples found no microorganisms linked to her professional activity, that observation was completed for 60% of contacts, that 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases were the only pathogens found among contacts, and reportedly that no infectious-disease medical consultations were registered among institute staff in the past 10 days. No absolute contact count was given.
The EU Health Security Committee discussed the suspected Russian plague case at an already-scheduled meeting in Brussels, with the item added to the agenda.
Regional authorities called a circulating claim that pregnant women in Irkutsk are being asked to fill in plague questionnaires a fake.

context.text: The institution is the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, a federal healthcare institution founded in 1934 and supervised by Rospotrebnadzor. Its remit covers plague and other dangerous infections, including cholera and anthrax.
Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, a bacterium found in small mammals and their fleas. It is a bacterium, not a virus.

Antibiotics work against the plague bacterium, so early diagnosis and treatment save lives. Treatment usually runs 10 to 14 days; ciprofloxacin, doxycycline and sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim are first-line options.
context.source_name: CDC MMWR, Antimicrobial Treatment and Prophylaxis of Plague (2021)

context.text: WHO gives the incubation period as one to seven days; CDC gives 1 to 3 days for the pneumonic form. The Russian health outlet Doctor Piter cited an incubation period of up to seven days on 3 October; no Irkutsk authority has published an incubation figure. CDC advises close contacts of a pneumonic case to take antibiotics for seven days and check their temperature twice daily for seven days.
context.source_name: WHO plague fact sheet; CDC Human Plague

context.text: Disambiguation: the Russian name for anthrax is 'сибирская язва', literally 'Siberian ulcer', sometimes rendered in English as 'Siberian plague'. Anthrax is caused by Bacillus anthracis and is unrelated to plague.

Laboratory-acquired plague infection is documented but rare: the Public Health Agency of Canada records at least 10 reported laboratory-acquired Yersinia pestis infections with 4 deaths. One is the 2009 Chicago case, in which a researcher died after infection with an attenuated vaccine strain.
context.source_name: Public Health Agency of Canada, Pathogen Safety Data Sheet: Yersinia pestis

watch.text: Rospotrebnadzor confirming or ruling out Yersinia pestis by name, rather than leaving the diagnosis as pneumonia of undetermined etiology. Russia told WHO on 6 October that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk, and Rospotrebnadzor has said expanded testing of her samples found no microorganisms linked to her professional activity, but no laboratory exclusion of Y. pestis for the deceased has been published and WHO says Russia has not named the pneumonia pathogen.
Russia telling WHO which pathogen caused the pneumonia. WHO asked on 6 October and had not been told as of the Geneva briefing.

Any contact under observation developing symptoms or returning a positive test for the pathogen. As of 5 October the only positives are 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus, which are incidental; Russia told WHO no high-threat pathogens were found among contacts.
The observation window ending. Rospotrebnadzor says observation ended for 60% of contacts as of 5 October. No official start or end date has been given for the remaining 40%.

A first official figure for contacts released from observation or discharged from hospital. Done in percentage form: Rospotrebnadzor said on 5 October that observation was completed for 60% of contacts.
An official absolute count of contacts, contacts released and contacts still under observation or in hospital, replacing the media-sourced 197 / 189 base and the derived 118 / 79 split.

The Irkutsk regional health ministry or Rospotrebnadzor confirming or denying the reported hospital measures in Irkutsk city. The regional government press service said on 5 October that all Irkutsk hospitals operate normally, and Rospotrebnadzor on 6 October denied region-wide restrictions; no regional health ministry statement has been found.
The Shelekhov district hospital inpatient department reopening. Regional media reported the quarantine still in force on 6 October; no reopening report found as of 7 October.
An official source naming the body investigating the Article 236 criminal case, or confirming the date it was opened.
An ECDC publication on the incident. Done: ECDC published a news item on 6 October.

A WHO Disease Outbreak News, ProMED, CIDRAP, UKHSA or CDC item on the incident. WHO has so far spoken only through a Director-General statement and spokesperson briefings (6 October), with graded risk levels but no Disease Outbreak News item.

A statement from the Anti-Plague Institute itself, the regional health ministry or the federal Health Ministry. Governor Kobzev said on 5 October that no new cases of institute staff seeking medical care had been identified, but the institute itself has not spoken.
The outcome of the EU Health Security Committee discussion on 7 October, if published.

unknowns: The cause of death is officially undetermined; Rospotrebnadzor has published no named laboratory results for the deceased and has neither named nor excluded Yersinia pestis. Russia's 6 October reply to WHO says no plague case has been recorded and the illness first presented as a typical acute respiratory viral infection, but WHO says Russia has not identified the pneumonia pathogen.
The exposure (25 Sep), symptom onset (27 Sep) and hospitalisation (29 Sep or 1 Oct) dates rest on media and Telegram sourcing; no official timeline exists.

Rospotrebnadzor has given only a percentage (60%) of contacts released from observation; no absolute release, discharge or remaining count has been published, so the figures of about 118 released and about 79 remaining are derived from the media-sourced 197 base.
No official end date for the observation period of the remaining contacts has been published.
The 197 / 189 contact figures trace to one outlet's unnamed sources, repeated by the regional government paper OGIRK and federal outlets; officials have published no count.

No number of contacts tested and no description of prophylaxis has been published; the only named results are 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases, and Russia told WHO no high-threat pathogens were found among contacts.

No statement from the Anti-Plague Institute itself, the regional health ministry or the federal Health Ministry; Governor Kobzev said on 5 October no new cases of institute staff seeking medical care were identified, and the Shkulev network reports Rospotrebnadzor saying no infectious-disease consultations among staff in 10 days, but the media-reported isolation of more than 60 staff has no official figure.

The scope of the Irkutsk city hospital measures is contested: the regional government press service (5 Oct) and fact-check outlets say hospitals operate normally, while The Insider, Meduza and Current Time report restrictions at several hospitals; Rospotrebnadzor's 6 October denial covers region-wide restrictions only, and the US Embassy alert refers to press reports of hospital closures.
A criminal case is reported under Article 236 of the Criminal Code; the investigating body and the date it was opened are unconfirmed.
The worker's name (Darya Shipilova) and age (reported as 27 or 28) are media-sourced and not officially confirmed.
The full three-tier WHO risk grading (moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for the WHO European Region) is reported by UN News but has not been seen in a WHO document.
No WHO Disease Outbreak News, UKHSA, ProMED, CIDRAP or CDC item as of 7 Oct; ECDC published a news item on 6 Oct and the EU Health Security Committee discussed the case on 7 Oct.
No Reuters or BBC item found; AP, CNN, NBC, CBC, CNBC, PBS, Euronews, Global News and a Bloomberg explainer exist.
